MEETING DATE:
10/20/2026

TOPIC:
Review Award of Contract for the Instructional Audit to Hanover Research for a Total Cost Not to Exceed
$255,000

POLICY ALIGNMENT:
DJ, Purchasing
DJ-R, Purchasing Regulation

BACKGROUND:
The instructional audit will provide an objective, division-wide assessment of how curriculum expectations,
instructional planning, assessment of student performance, and classroom practices align to support student
learning in English language arts and mathematics.

RATIONALE:
Building on WJCC Schools’ investments in high-quality instructional materials and professional learning, the
audit will identify effective practices, opportunities for greater consistency, and targeted supports to strengthen
instruction, inform the Teaching and Learning Framework, and accelerate student achievement.

SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
The request for school board consideration and action on October 20 will allow the division to move forward
with project planning and maintain the anticipated timeline for the audit. The proposed contract will be
awarded through the Virginia Association of State College and University Purchasing Professionals
(VASCUPP) cooperative contract GMU-1827-23-07, held by George Mason University and available for use by
WJCC Schools in accordance with school board purchasing policies and regulations.

COST BUDGETED:
The budget request to approve the award of contract for the instructional audit to Hanover Research is for a
total cost not to exceed $255,000.00. Funding will consist of $100,000 from the $427,000 in one-time additional
state revenue set aside by the school board in the FY27 amended budget approved in August 2026 for non-
recurring expenditures, with the remaining $155,000 funded through a budget transfer from instructional salary
and benefit savings.

ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.

SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board review the proposed award of contract to Hanover Research under
VASCUPP cooperative contract GMU-1827-23-07 and the associated budget transfer, and be prepared to vote
later in the same meeting on October 20, 2026.

items.title: Approval of Resolution R-21-26, National School Psychology Week
items.body:
TOPIC:
Approve Resolution R-21-26, National School Psychology Week
BACKGROUND:
The Virginia Department of Education has joined with the Virginia Academy of School Psychologists in
celebrating National School Psychology Week, November 9-13, 2026. Schools will highlight the role of school
psychology and school-based services in promoting student success.
RATIONALE:
School psychologists work with students, general and special educators, parents, administrators, and allied
professionals to create safe, healthy, and supportive learning environments focused on collaboration,
cooperation, and achievement. School psychologists work to engage students at all levels of learning and
development to promote personal achievement, growth, and resilience, as well as a sense of connectedness
and wellbeing. The resolution wording is recommended by the National Association for School Psychologists.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board approve Resolution R-21-26 declaring that November 9-13, 2026
be recognized as National School Psychology Week.
DATA SOURCE:
Adam Brown, Ed.D., Chief Operating Officer
Brooke Crews, Director of Special Education
RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Move to approve the consent agenda as presented.

items.title: Approval of Award of Contract for Request for Proposal #20261032, Engineering Service for Matoaka Elementary HVAC Replacement
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/20/2026
TOPIC:
Approve the Award of Contract for Request for Proposal #20261032, Engineering Service for Matoaka
Elementary HVAC Replacement to PACE Collaborative, for a Total Cost of $342,513
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
BBA, School Board Powers and Duties
BACKGROUND:
The current HVAC system at Matoaka Elementary was installed in 2007 and has reached the end of its useful
life. Williamsburg-James City County Public Schools solicited sealed proposals from qualified
architecture/engineering firms to produce detailed designs, construction drawings, specifications and contract
documents, and to obtain the necessary related regulatory approvals for replacement of the heating ventilating
and air conditioning (HVAC) system at Matoaka Elementary School. It is the intent of this proposal to result in
the competitive negotiation of a fixed price contract for these services. The successful firm will demonstrate
proven management skills and technical competence in the design of HVAC systems of similar design and
function. It is anticipated that the required design services will include Architectural and Mechanical, Plumbing,
Electrical and Structural Engineering.
The project includes:
• Replacement of four-pipe induction units, make-up air units, hydronic air handling units, split systems,
exhaust fans, air-cooled chillers, boilers, automated HVAC controls, and electrical components
associated with the HVAC system.
• Re-use existing ductwork and piping to the greatest extent possible. Cleaning and sealing of ductwork.
An RFP was issued on May 15, 2026, with a due date of June 12, 2026. Notice of the RFP was posted
Euna/OpenBids and placed on the James City County website.
RATIONALE:
N/A
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
The adopted FY26 Capital Improvement Plan includes a total project budget of $480,000. The total cost of the
HVAC Design Fee is $342,513.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.



SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board approve the award of contract for the Matoaka Elementary HVAC
replacement to PACE Collaborative, for a total cost of $342,513.
DATA SOURCE:
Marcellus Snipes, Senior Director for Operations
RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Move to approve the award of contract for the Matoaka Elementary HVAC replacement to PACE Collaborative,
for a total cost of $342,513.

items.title: Approval of Award of Contract for Instructional Audit
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/20/2026
TOPIC:
Approve Award of Contract for the Instructional Audit to Hanover Research for a Total Cost Not to Exceed
$255,000 and the Associated Budget Transfer
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
DJ, Purchasing
DJ-R, Purchasing Regulation
BACKGROUND:
The instructional audit will provide an objective, division-wide assessment of how curriculum expectations,
instructional planning, assessment of student performance, and classroom practices align to support student
learning in English language arts and mathematics.
RATIONALE:
Building on WJCC Schools’ investments in high-quality instructional materials and professional learning, the
audit will identify effective practices, opportunities for greater consistency, and targeted supports to strengthen
instruction, inform the Teaching and Learning Framework, and accelerate student achievement.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
The request for school board consideration and action on October 20 will allow the division to move forward
with project planning and maintain the anticipated timeline for the audit. The proposed contract will be
awarded through the Virginia Association of State College and University Purchasing Professionals
(VASCUPP) cooperative contract GMU-1827-23-07, held by George Mason University and available for use by
WJCC Schools in accordance with school board purchasing policies and regulations.
COST BUDGETED:
The budget request to approve the award of contract for the instructional audit to Hanover Research is for a
total cost not to exceed $255,000.00. Funding will consist of $100,000 from the $427,000 in one-time additional
state revenue set aside by the school board in the FY27 amended budget approved in August 2026 for nonrecurring expenditures, with the remaining $155,000 funded through a budget transfer from instructional salary
and benefit savings.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board approve the award of contract to Hanover Research under
VASCUPP cooperative contract GMU-1827-23-07 for a total cost not to exceed $255,000 and approve the
associated budget transfer.

items.title: Approval of Superintendent's Recommendation for School Division Redistricting
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/20/2026
TOPIC:
Approval of Superintendent's Recommendation for School Division Redistricting
BACKGROUND:
Many school buildings in WJCC Schools, specifically at the elementary level, are at capacity. To accommodate
student population, eight of nine WJCC elementary schools have portable classrooms (trailers) on site. With the
anticipated August 2027 occupancy of two new pre-k centers, the school division must also consider the best and
most efficient way to utilize elementary space that will be available when pre-k students are located in the new pre-k
spaces, instead of in the five elementary schools that currently host the pre-k program. The shift will leave some
elementary spaces unoccupied while other spaces remain at or over capacity. Engaging in conversation on school
zones also allows the school division to consider boundaries, feeder pattern alignment, efficiencies, and effective
delivery at the secondary level.
RATIONALE:
The Redistricting Steering Committee released draft attendance zone maps for each level on May 12, 2026, and
revisions were presented on August 4, 2026. Community members engaged in two feedback processes. The
Redistricting Steering Committee presented a final map recommendation to Dr. Keever on September 1, 2026. Dr.
Keever then presented his recommendation to the school board on September 15, 2026. In addition to public
comment opportunities during Regular Meetings, a public hearing was held on October 6, 2026.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
N/A
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends that the board approve the redistricted school division attendance zones as
presented.
DATA SOURCE:
Daniel Keever, Ph.D., Superintendent
Kara Wall, Chief Communications Officer
